candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; understand expected medication actions/outcomes; provide medication education and safely manage prescribed therapies.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — recognition of guideline-directed multidrug therapy for HFrEF
candidate.educational_objective: Identify the four foundational HFrEF medication classes: renin-angiotensin system inhibition with ARNI/ACE inhibitor/ARB, an evidence-based beta blocker, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.

options.A: Sacubitril/valsartan, metoprolol succinate extended-release, spironolactone, and dapagliflozin.
options.D: Metoprolol tartrate, diltiazem, furosemide, and aspirin.

candidate.rationale: The AHA/ACC/HFSA HFrEF guideline organizes foundational pharmacologic therapy around renin-angiotensin system inhibition with an ARNI, ACE inhibitor, or ARB; an evidence-based beta blocker; a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; and an SGLT2 inhibitor. Option A supplies one appropriate representative from each class: sacubitril/valsartan, sustained-release metoprolol succinate, spironolactone, and dapagliflozin. B contains useful drugs in selected circumstances but not the four foundational classes; C combines overlapping renin-angiotensin drugs rather than four distinct classes; and D substitutes medications not comprising the recommended foundational HFrEF regimen.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports the four foundational HFrEF pharmacologic categories and the selected representative agents used in the correct regimen.
candidate.source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: Section 7.3, Pharmacological Treatment for HFrEF: 7.3.1 renin-angiotensin system inhibition with ACEi/ARB/ARNI; 7.3.2 evidence-based beta blockers; 7.3.3 mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists; 7.3.4 SGLT2 inhibitors. Professional Heart Daily 'Top Things to Know' states HFrEF GDMT includes four medication classes, including SGLT2 inhibitors.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
candidate.stem: A client has symptomatic chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Assuming no contraindications and that each drug is clinically appropriate, which regimen contains one agent from each of the four foundational medication classes recommended in current HFrEF guideline-directed therapy?
